references.text: Samson went down to Timnah and saw a woman there among the daughters of the Philistines, whom he later married.
Samson's wife was given to his companion, which explains why he was not allowed to go in to her afterward.
The wheat harvest is mentioned as a specific time of year, just as in Samson's story.
The wheat harvest was an important festival in Israel and marked a particular time of the year.
The father's explanation for giving away Samson's wife and his offer of the younger sister.
A young goat was used as a gift or payment, just as Samson brought a young goat to his wife.
